title: Optimize metric emission path for perf-canary high-frequency sampling
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: perf-canary sampling is intentionally frequent (per-model/region slices) and we saw measurable overhead in the request hot path from metric event construction + label handling. This PR introduces a fast-path for canary-tagged metric emission: fewer allocations, less string churn, and a more explicit label policy so we stay within cardinality budgets while still attaching the debug context we need. Changes: (1) Replace per-event HashMap label building with a pre-interned LabelSet (smallvec-backed) keyed off a CanopyLabelPolicy; (2) Add a thread-local MetricEventBuffer to batch writes to the emitter on flush boundaries (end of request / stream close) instead of emitting every intermediate counter immediately; (3) Avoid repeated formatting of runtime_build/scheduler_mode by storing interned IDs (string only at export); (4) Convert canary "source=perf-canary" to a compact request tag bit and plumb it through MetricContext so the branch is predictable; (5) Add microbench + a pprof note to the perf-canary docs. Risk: correctness regressions (missed labels or wrong aggregation) and accidental label drops; this includes unit tests asserting label schema + a golden snapshot of exported series for a representative canary request. Rollout: safe to land; canary tag gates the fast path so impact should be limited to canary traffic, with a fallback to the old path behind METRICS_FASTPATH_DISABLE=1 for quick rollback.
commits: telemetry: add LabelSet + interned string table for canary fast-path
telemetry: batch metric events via thread-local buffer + flush hooks
runtime: plumb canary request tag bit into MetricContext
tests: golden export snapshot + label schema assertions for canary series
bench: add microbench for MetricEventBuilder (old vs new)
docs: perf profiling notes + guidance for disabling fast-path
perf_profiling_notes: Baseline (main @ 6f1b3a9, us-east A10G, canary runner @ 5 rps/model slice): telemetry emission accounted for ~3.4% CPU in the runtime process during steady-state decode-heavy workload, with top stacks in MetricEventBuilder::with_label (HashMap growth) and fmt::format (runtime_build/scheduler_mode). After this change (head @ 9c2d4e1): telemetry emission ~0.7–1.0% CPU; allocations in the hot path dropped from ~28 allocs/request to ~6 allocs/request for canary-tagged requests (remaining allocs largely in tracing span fields, not metrics). Note: if METRICS_EXPORT_STRING_INTERN=0 (debug mode) the win is smaller (~1.6% CPU) since we bypass the intern table.
review_summary: Approved after tightening label allowlist semantics, adding an explicit fallback/kill-switch, and demonstrating the CPU/alloc delta with microbench + pprof. SRE asked to ensure buffered emit doesn’t delay alerting beyond the window; flush points were confirmed at end-of-request and stream close, so time-to-ingest remains effectively unchanged for canary workloads.
review_comments: Logan Wright: Can we guarantee we’re not silently dropping required labels (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build) in the new label policy? Please add a test that fails if any required label is missing in exported series.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added canary_metrics_schema_test.rs with an explicit required label set and a golden snapshot of exported series for (streaming + non-streaming). The test fails if required labels are missing or if disallowed labels appear.
Thomas Baird: I like the allowlist, but please document the cardinality rationale. Also, ensure the intern table can’t grow without bound if someone adds request IDs by mistake.

Caleb Johnson (author): Updated label_policy.rs docs with the cardinality budget + examples of forbidden labels. Intern table now only accepts labels from the policy enum; arbitrary strings can’t be interned without code changes.

Nadia Rahman: Buffered emission worries me for streaming—do we still get accurate tokens/sec and latency histograms if we only flush at the end? Any risk of missing mid-stream counters on cancellation?

Caleb Johnson (author): For streaming, we flush on both normal stream close and cancellation/abort paths (stream_lifecycle.rs). tokens/sec uses timestamps captured in-request; metrics are emitted once with correct values, so buffering doesn’t change semantics.
Sean Gallagher: Please add a kill switch so oncall can revert without a full rollback if we see unexpected metric gaps during rollout.

Caleb Johnson (author): Added METRICS_FASTPATH_DISABLE=1 to force old path (guarded in emitter.rs). Also added a runtime log line at startup indicating which path is active for canary-tagged requests.
Allison Grant: Minor: naming—prefer 'label_schema' over 'label_policy' in docs, but code is fine. Also ensure this doesn’t change any non-canary metric series.
Caleb Johnson (author): Docs updated to call out label schema explicitly; code path is gated on request tag bit so non-canary series are unchanged.
release_notes: Internal: Reduce runtime overhead of perf-canary metric emission by adding a canary-gated fast path (buffered emit + interned label sets). No expected impact to customer traffic metrics.
